title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability & Performance
author: Alicia Morgan
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, and performance. It defines mandatory conventions, ownership, and the process for creating and recording Architecture Decision Records (ADRs). The goal is a predictable, auditable, and maintainable platform that meets our latency, cost, and reliability objectives.

Scope:
- Applies to all services and libraries owned by Engineering teams that are expected to be deployed in hosted, dedicated, or private modes.
- Includes SDKs, control-plane components, runtime serving components, and deployment automation (Terraform/Helm/Ansible).

Owners and Contacts:
- Standards Owner: Eng Architecture (eng-architecture@redwood.example.com)
- API Standards Owner: API Platform (owner: Priya Desai)
- Infra/IaC Owner: Cloud Infra (owner: Lucas Chen)
- Model-serving Owner: Serving Runtime (owner: Ravi Patel)
- Observability / SRE Owner: Eng SRE (owner: Maria Gomez)

1) API Standards
Purpose: Ensure consistent, discoverable, and backwards-compatible surface area for clients (internal and external).

Key rules:
- API style: OpenAPI v3 for REST endpoints; gRPC for high-throughput internal RPCs. All public REST endpoints must publish an OpenAPI spec in the repo root at "openapi.yaml".
- URL design: use nouns, kebab-case, versioned base path: /v1/, /v2/ (e.g. /v1/models/{model_id}/infer). Avoid verbs in resource paths.
- Versioning: Major version in path (v1). Minor/patch backward-compatible changes via headers and feature flags. Deprecation window: 90 days for public APIs unless security fixes.
- Auth: All APIs use OAuth2 bearer tokens for external customers; internal service-to-service calls use mTLS + short-lived JWTs. Document the auth flow in API spec.
- Request/Response conventions:
  - Use 200 for success with structured JSON payloads; use 202 for async acceptance with Location header.
  - Errors use RFC 7807 Problem Details with fields: type, title, status, detail, instance, and optional error_code.
  - Pagination: use cursor-based pagination for large lists with next_cursor and page_size.
- Rate limiting: return 429 with Retry-After header. Include X-RateLimit-{Limit,Remaining,Reset} headers on responses.
- Idempotency: POST endpoints that create resources must accept an Idempotency-Key header and store previous results for 24 hours.
- Documentation: Every public endpoint must have examples (curl + SDK) in the API spec and a short usage guide in the service README.

API Review Checklist (required before merge):
1. OpenAPI file present and validated (swagger-cli validate).
2. Auth and scopes documented.
3. Error schema uses Problem Details.
4. Load test notes included if endpoint will receive >100 RPS.
5. Client SDK compatibility tests (unit) exist.

2) Coding Standards
Purpose: Reduce cognitive overhead across the codebase, enable automated checks, and improve review quality.

General rules (all languages):
- Use the repository-level linter and formatter configuration. No manual style changes in PRs.
- All code must include unit tests and where appropriate integration tests. Test coverage: core libraries >= 70%.
- Commit messages: follow Conventional Commits (type(scope): subject).
- PR size: Prefer PRs < 400 lines of change; large changes require a design doc and ADR.

Language-specific highlights:
- Go: gofmt, go vet, errcheck enabled in CI. Public packages must have doc comments and examples.
- Python: Black + isort + mypy in pre-commit. Use type annotations for public functions.
- Rust: rustfmt, clippy in CI.
- Typescript: eslint with airbnb ruleset extended; prefer readonly types for public interfaces.

Security & secrets:
- No secrets in code or config. Use secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault).
- Dependabot: auto-PRs enabled for critical/high CVEs; teams must triage within 5 business days.

3) Infrastructure (IaC) Standards
Purpose: Make infrastructure changes auditable, repeatable, and safe across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Rules:
- Primary IaC: Terraform for cloud resources; Helm for k8s manifests; Ansible only for onprem packaging tasks.
- Module reuse: Share common modules from infra-modules repo. No hard-coded account IDs or regions in modules.
- Tagging: All resources must include tags: owner_team, service, environment, cost_center, created_by.
- State: Remote state must use backend with encryption (S3 + DynamoDB lock for AWS) or cloud equivalent.
- Secrets: Use KMS envelope encryption and do not store plaintext secrets in state. Use encrypted SSM/Secrets Manager or Vault.
- Network: VPCs must be defined per environment with standardized egress/ingress rules. Private deployments must follow reference-architecture (see reference-architectures/onprem-vpc).
- Change management: Any plan that changes >3 production resources or modifies networking requires a peer review + infra-canary runbook and an approved infra change ticket.

Deployment process:
1. Branch + Terraform plan in CI that runs against a temporary workspace.
2. Apply allowed only via pipeline with manual approval for production.
3. Post-apply smoke tests + alerting.

4) Model-Serving Standards
Purpose: Ensure model artifacts are versioned, reproducible, and served with predictable performance and rollback capability.

Model artifact rules:
- Packaging: Model artifacts (weights + config + tokenizer) must be stored in model-registry with semantic versioning (semver-style: major.minor.patch). Include metadata: framework, quantization_profile, float_size, tokenizer_version, hash.
- Quantization profiles: Maintain quantization-profiles directory in confluence applied-ml-and-evals. Each profile must include expected perf/quality tradeoffs and recommended workloads.
- Containerization: Serving images must be built from standardized base images and include health checks, /metrics, /ready endpoints.

Runtime rules:
- KV cache management: Runtime must expose cache stats (hits, misses, eviction_count) via Prometheus metrics.
- Backpressure: Model server should reject (429) or queue with configured max_queue_ms when overloaded; documented behavior in service README.
- Compatibility: When a new model variant is introduced, runtime must advertise compatibility tags allowing routing layer to fallback if needed.
- Canary deploys: Default rollout for model version is 10% -> 50% -> 100% with quality gating. Automated rollback if quality regressions exceed thresholds.

Model test & evaluation:
- Ship unit prompt tests with every model. Maintain a canonical prompt-set for canary quality checks.
- Regression threshold: automatic rollback if regression in top-line eval metric > 2% absolute or if latency P95 increases by > 20% vs baseline.

5) Observability Standards
Purpose: Ensure that all services are observable with consistent metrics, traces, and logs to enable fast debugging and SLO verification.

Metrics:
- Use Prometheus client libraries. Metrics naming convention: <service>_<resource>_<metric>_{total|duration_seconds|count}. Avoid high-cardinality labels (no user_id, request_id as a label).
- Required metrics: request_count, request_errors (4xx,5xx), latency_seconds (histogram), concurrency_in_flight, resource_utilization (gpu_utilization, cpu_usage).
- Cardinality: restrict label values to <100 unique values for any given metric.

Tracing:
- Use OpenTelemetry. Span naming: {service}.{operation} (e.g., inference.generate). Include trace_id and span_id in logs for correlation.
- Trace sampling: default 10% for production; 100% sample for errors.

Logging:
- JSON structured logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, environment, trace_id, span_id, msg, error_code, request_id.
- Sensitive fields redacted before writing to logs.

Dashboards & Alerts:
- Standard dashboards: service overview, latency heatmap, error budget burn, resource usage. Template dashboards live in dashboards-and-alerts repo.
- Alerting policy: use SLO-driven alerts (see SLO table below). Alert severity and paging rules defined in eng-sre/runbooks.

6) Performance Standards & SLOs
SLOs are the primary contract between platform and consumers. All services must define SLOs and a corresponding alerting policy.

SLO table (examples):
| Service | SLI | Target (90d) | Alert threshold (page) | Owner |
|---------|-----|--------------:|----------------------:|-------|
| API Gateway | availability (200 responses) | 99.95% | < 99.9% | Eng SRE |
| Inference Runtime (hosted) | p95 latency (token generation) | 250 ms | p95 > 300 ms for 15m | Serving Runtime |
| Embeddings API | availability | 99.9% | < 99.5% | API Platform |

Performance requirements and benchmarking:
- Benchmarks must be reproducible with the benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Include load profile, hardware spec, dataset/sample prompts.
- All model-serving PRs that change kernels/quantization must include perf and quality numbers and an explicit comparison vs baseline.
- Target throughput calculations: provide RPS-to-GPU mapping guidance in gpu-fleet-and-capacity.

7) Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) Process
- New ADR required when a design decision has broad impact (infra topology, auth model, major API surface change, model-serving architecture).
- ADR template (must live in repo docs/adr): title, status, context, decision, consequences, alternatives considered, owners, date.
- ADR lifecycle: draft -> in_review -> published. Keep ADRs concise and link to design docs and CI artifacts.
- Example ADRs: use of OpenTelemetry (link), selection of Terraform + Helm, decision to use semantic model versions.

ADR Review checklist:
1. Impact analysis included (teams, rollback path, cost).
2. Proposed migrations and compatibility windows documented.
3. Sign-off by affected owners.

8) Operational Playbooks and Runbooks
- Every service must have a concise runbook: symptoms, remediation steps, dashboards to check, escalation path, and postmortem link. Runbooks live under eng-platform/runbooks and oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks.
- Incident response: follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process. Postmortems are required for Sev-1 and Sev-2 incidents.

9) Governance and Exceptions
- Exceptions to these standards require a documented risk assessment and an approved exception ticket. Exceptions are temporary and reviewed quarterly.
- Standards are reviewed annually by Eng Architecture and updated with changelog.

10) Appendix: Example Checklists and Commands
OpenAPI validation example:
  swagger-cli validate openapi.yaml

Terraform plan example (CI):
  terraform init -backend-config=...
  terraform plan -var-file=env.prod.tfvars

Model artifact metadata example (YAML):
  name: redwood-bert-1b
  version: 1.3.0
  framework: pytorch
  quantization_profile: q4_1
  float_size: float16
  tokenizer_version: 2025-10-01
  hash: sha256:abcdef...

PR checklist (required):
- [ ] Title follows Conventional Commits
- [ ] Unit tests + CI green
- [ ] Linter & formatter passed
- [ ] OpenAPI present (if applicable)
- [ ] Metrics & tracing added for new endpoints
- [ ] Load/perf notes included (if applicable)
- [ ] Security review completed for public endpoints

Change log highlights (recent):
- 2026-03-05: Added explicit P95 latency SLO for inference runtime and requirement for canary quality gating.
- 2025-12-01: Standardized on OpenTelemetry tracing and Prometheus metrics naming.
